decision: YES -- STANDING APPROVAL GRANTED TO THE CONDUCTOR, AND IT DOES NOT REPEAL THE NO-AUTO-REFILL RULING. (2) WHAT DID NOT CHANGE -- the reap-and-document beat is still mandatory. Every arrow is still a stop; what Joshua has delegated is the approval step, not the reaping or the documenting. (3) STILL FORBIDDEN -- machine auto-dispatch. refill-idle-panes --apply remains refused at the top of run() with APPROVAL_REQUIRED detector=actuation_withheld (verified live at 05cdd2a); no cron row dispatches into this repo (50 uncommitted rows, zero matching); ai.zeststream.omp-orchestrator.plist remains loaded ZERO times while only the control-plane variant runs. WHY THE DELEGATION IS SAFE NOW AND WAS NOT YESTERDAY: the notification half is measured working. inbox-monitor was installed and given a blocking --watch (abebf10), and on 2026-09-04 at 16:29Z a real pane completion woke a blocked conductor after 49 polls / 496s with no human involved -- the first closed loop of the project. decision: TEAM DECISION, taken under Joshua's 2026-09-05 delegation. CHOICE: schedule fleet-monitor ONLY, and only with its own --state path; reap-finished-panes and refill-idle-panes are NOT scheduled. REASONS, each measured. A one-shot sweep needs a CALLER; putting a sweep on a timer is not the same as giving it a caller, and only fleet-monitor is genuinely periodic (one attention tick, and it is the only scheduled writer of the standing admission verdict). (2) refill-idle-panes --apply STAYS REFUSED regardless of any schedule, under Joshua's 2026-09-03 no-auto-refill ruling recorded in CONTRACT.md Wave 3 and HD-0015: 'we dont want to automatically refill panes with work without being approved'. Its --plan lane is a proposal and already emits APPROVAL_REQUIRED detector=actuation-withheld; scheduling a proposal nobody reads would reproduce the exact defect this session measured twice. (3) THE OVERLAP TRAP IS MEASURED, NOT THEORETICAL: pane 4 reported OVERLAP_VERDICT=overlaps:tick-monitor-observe-vs-fleet-monitor-admission-verdict, and this session independently produced LEDGER CONTENDED when two watchers shared the default tick-monitor ledger -- one watcher's last_tick advanced on the wrong cadence and silently disabled the two-capture liveness rule, reporting gap_secs_too_short as no error. A schedule without a reader manufactures a file that grows. fleet-monitor's reader is the standing admission verdict that controller-tick consumes, which is why it is the one that qualifies. NOT DECIDED HERE and left open: the schedule INTERVAL. Joshua's own measured discipline applies -- this session derived a wake bound from observed completion times (median 10 min, max 16, bound = max + 50%) rather than picking a round number, and the same method should set this interval from observed attention-tick need rather than a guess. Until that measurement exists the interval is UNKNOWN, and an unmeasured interval is not a schedule.

question: Adopt SPLIT ACCEPTANCE for graded beads -- a visible set the implementer receives plus a held-out composition set it never sees, with the grader reporting the pass-rate gap as a number? Source-verified basis: arXiv:2605.21384 (SpecBench) measures our exact architecture -- 'oversight collapses onto a single surface: the automated test suite' -- and finds every frontier agent saturates the visible suite while the held-out gap grows 28 percentage points per tenfold increase in code size; this workspace is 72 members and ~133k LOC. Our mutation leg proves a test is ATTRIBUTABLE (it caught a guard invisible to 63/63 tests tonight) but not that an implementation GENERALISES past the suite it was handed. Cost: acceptance authorship doubles, and the held-out set may not be written by the implementer, extending R6 from closure to acceptance. Recommendation from pane 1: ADOPT for P0/P1 beads only, measure the gap on ten graded beads, and drop it if visible and held-out pass rates prove identical -- which would mean the held-out set composes nothing.
decision: ADOPT, SCOPED: split acceptance -- a visible set the implementer receives plus a held-out composition set it never sees -- is ADOPTED for beads whose acceptance is a MEASUREMENT (censuses, gates, classifiers), and NOT adopted for beads whose acceptance is a BEHAVIOUR change. Rationale from tonight's measured evidence: every acceptance-runner defect found today was in a measurement bead, and three of them were defects in the acceptance's OWN command -- the literal `rg -c ... | wc -l` returning the glob size (227 for every field, including a needle that cannot match), R7's `d.get('id')` resolving set() unconditionally, and a ledger parser accepting any id. A held-out set catches exactly that class, because the implementer cannot tune to a runner it has not seen. For behaviour beads the visible acceptance IS the spec, and hiding half of it re-creates the dispatch-only-instruction defect.
evidence: Measured 2026-09-07, three acceptance-runner defects in one session, all in measurement beads: xv5r's literal `rg -c ... | wc -l` was a CONSTANT (227) because `rg -c` emits path:0 rows so `wc -l` returns the glob size; control `git grep -c` returned 23/32/0.
R7's runner clause `{d['id'] for d in ... if d.get('id')}` resolved set() unconditionally -- correct for `br show --json`, pointed at the jsonl, and the two key sets share ZERO names.
A ledger parser accepted any id, found by %20.

Counter-evidence for the behaviour-bead exclusion: AGENTS.md's 'A DISPATCH-ONLY INSTRUCTION IS AN UNRECORDED REQUIREMENT' -- a requirement the grader cannot see is invisible to verification by construction.
no_claim: Split acceptance raises the cost of every graded bead and does not detect a held-out set that is itself wrong -- it moves the single point of failure from the implementer to the author of the held-out legs. It also cannot be applied retroactively to beads already dispatched. Unmeasured: whether the held-out set actually catches anything the visible one misses; that needs a trial on the next measurement bead before this is generalised.
condition: Applies to measurement beads dispatched after 2026-09-07. A bead may opt out with a written reason in its acceptance. If the first trial shows the held-out set catching nothing the visible set missed, this reverts.
review_after: the first three measurement beads graded under split acceptance
